turns.content: The court is convened on 'Certification Ready'. The advocates are HR, Learning & Development, Managers. Each will argue its own definition; the divergence will be settled by executed evidence, and a canonical meaning will be published only if a configured owner may approve it.
For HR: 80 are ready. My definition is Learner has completed every required learning module for the certification. I have executed it over the grounded population and stand on that result.

For Learning & Development: 56 are ready. My definition is Learner has completed every required module and the latest practice assessment score is at least 80 percent. I have executed it over the grounded population and stand on that result.
For Managers: 56 are ready. My definition is Learner has completed every required lab and has a recorded manager approval. I have executed it over the grounded population and stand on that result.

Plan: HR, Learning & Development, Managers disagree. Hypothesis — the divergence sits where one owner's gate admits learners another owner blocks. I will execute each definition and subtract the set every definition agrees on to isolate the contested cohort.
Executed. 24 learners are claimed ready by one owner but false-ready learners (for example L057, L058, L059). At 10,800 exam spend at risk, the divergence is material.
Replan: confirm the contested cohort is exactly the looser definition minus the stricter one. Confirmed — 24 learners, no more, no fewer.

Cross-examination of HR: you claim 80 ready, but some are outside the set every definition agrees on (for example L001, L002, L003). Concede that your count is a claim under your own gate, not enterprise readiness — or produce evidence.

Cross-examination of Learning & Development: you claim 56 ready, but some are outside the set every definition agrees on (for example L001, L002, L003). Concede that your count is a claim under your own gate, not enterprise readiness — or produce evidence.

Cross-examination of Managers: you claim 56 ready, but some are outside the set every definition agrees on (for example L057, L058, L059). Concede that your count is a claim under your own gate, not enterprise readiness — or produce evidence.

HR responds: conceded. My population is correct under my mandate, but I yield that it is not the enterprise readiness term. I defend my scope as a named domain view and accept that the canonical meaning must be governed.

Learning & Development responds: conceded. My population is correct under my mandate, but I yield that it is not the enterprise readiness term. I defend my scope as a named domain view and accept that the canonical meaning must be governed.

Managers responds: conceded. My population is correct under my mandate, but I yield that it is not the enterprise readiness term. I defend my scope as a named domain view and accept that the canonical meaning must be governed.

Reflection: 3 claim(s) were conceded as claims, not readiness. No count was accepted on argument — each is the row count of an executed query recorded as evidence. The debate is resolved; what remains is who, if anyone, may approve a canonical.
Authority is clear. Learning Governance Council is the configured owner and may approve a canonical definition. The court may publish a governed proposal for human approval.
Ruling: the divergence is proven and a configured owner may approve. The court publishes a governed canonical proposal that still requires human approval.
